newsitem.title: USA: Dudley Moore and wife reconcile; she drops lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Dudley Moore and wife reconcile; she drops lawsuit.

text.p: Oscar-nominated actor Dudley Moore has reconciled with his estranged wife and she has dropped a lawsuit alleging he abused her, the comedian's lawyer said on Friday.
The announcement came less than a month after Nicole Moore's lawyers had said she was adding more allegations to the suit she filed in May.
"He and Mrs Moore have reconciled and resolved all their differences," attorney Allan Sigel told reporters.
Sigel was in a Los Angeles courthouse where he was representing another client -- Harry Perzigian, who has sued actor Carroll O'Connor for slander.

Moore, 62, and his wife, who is 29 years younger, sat hand-in-hand in the courtroom for a while, listening to testimony in the O'Connor case. Their only connection with the trial was because Sigel is also Moore's lawyer.
Neither the English-born actor nor his wife, who were married in April 1994, made any comment to reporters.

Moore filed for divorce from his fourth wife in June 1996 and she responded in May 1997 with a lawsuit alleging the "Arthur" star choked her, kicked her, forced her to take stimulants and dance for him semi-nude.
Three weeks ago she added more allegations, including a claim that Moore "viciously grabbed (his wife's) breast only days after she had breast implant surgery."
A month before they were married in 1994, Moore was arrested for what he later described as "a domestic tiff." Prosecutors filed no charges.

The accomplished jazz and classical pianist rose to fame in satirical stage reviews in England and on British television with his friend from Oxford University, Peter Cook. He later moved to the United States and became a household name after starring opposite Bo Derek in the 1979 comedy "10".
He was nominated for a best actor Academy Award in 1981 for playing a drunken millionaire in "Arthur".
